predecessors.name: Spanish Empire
predecessors.text: Curaçao, whose Spanish defenders surrendered at San Juan in August 1634

successors.name: Netherlands
successors.text: Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, special municipalities of the Netherlands from 10 October 2010

successors.name: curacao
successors.text: Curaçao, a constituent country of the Kingdom from 10 October 2010

successors.name: Sint Maarten
successors.text: Sint Maarten, a constituent country from 10 October 2010

successors.name: aruba
successors.text: Aruba, a separate country within the Kingdom since 1 January 1986

ledger.x: 1634: the Dutch take Curaçao.
1636: Aruba and Bonaire.
1636: Sint Eustatius, its only town Oranjestad later sacked by the British (1781).
1640: Saba.
1648: Saint Martin is divided.
1800: the British take Curaçao.
1803: Curaçao returns to the Dutch after the British three-year hold; 'They attacked again in 1804'.
1807: the second British occupation begins: 'They attacked again in 1804, and then held it from 1807 to 1816.'
1815: 'From 1815 onwards Curaçao and Dependencies formed a colony of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.'
1816: the British hand Curaçao back 'under the terms of the Treaty of Paris'.
1828: one West Indies colony.
1828: the merged colony is governed from Paramaribo, not Willemstad.
1845: Suriname leaves.
1845: Willemstad is the capital again; the Dutch part of the SSS islands now belongs to Curaçao and Dependencies, with Willemstad as its capital.
1936: 'Between 1936 and 1948, the area was officially known as the Territory of Curaçao.'
1948 (May): 'a new constitution for the territory entered into force' and it was 'renamed "Netherlands Antilles"'.
1986 (1 January): Aruba becomes a separate country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands, 'status aparte' after a 1977 consultative referendum.
2010 (10 October): Curaçao becomes a country.
2010 (10 October): Sint Maarten becomes a country (the Dutch half of Saint Martin).
2010 (10 October): the BES islands join the Netherlands as special municipalities.
2010 (10 October): 'The country was dissolved on 10 October 2010.'

wars.name: British occupation of Curaçao
wars.outcome: British captured Curaçao in 1800 and held it until 1803, attacked again in 1804 and held it from 1807 to 1816, returning it under the Treaty of Paris.

certainty.note: Small settlements in contested waters (Spain held the surrounding islands); the islands' extent is the island, but the hold on Aruba, Bonaire and Saba is the page's 'settled' only.
Islands bounded by their coasts, and the one land frontier, on Saint Martin (split with France 'in 1648'), is a treaty line.
